hints: The first split of interval [l,r] costs its sum.
The interval DP adds optimal costs of the two resulting pieces.
Knuth optimization bounds each best split between the best splits of two neighboring intervals.
analogy: A whole piece pays once to split, then each child piece is solved independently.
example: For [1,2,3], split [1,2] from [3] for cost 6, then split [1,2] for 3: total 9.
algorithm: Let dp[l][r]=sum(l..r)+min over l<=p<r of dp[l][p]+dp[p+1][r], with zero for singletons. Use prefix sums and Knuth optimization: search p only from opt[l][r-1] through opt[l+1][r], clipped to valid splits. Fill by increasing interval length and use wide arithmetic.
correctness: The recurrence enumerates every possible first split. Nonnegative interval sums satisfy the quadrangle and monotonicity conditions for Knuth optimization, so an optimal split lies in the stated range; induction then gives optimal interval costs.
complexity: For n values, O(n^2) time and O(n^2) space.
